title: Dendropanax proteus root and its major bio-phytochemicals alleviate rheumatoid arthritis by inhibiting TLR4/CLEC1B/PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB pathways: proteomics, metabolomics, collagen-induced arthritis rats, MH7A cells, molecular docking, and molecular dynamic simulation.
authors: Yang, Li; Yang, Yating; Wang, Qihui; Liang, Jian; Zhang, Shengyuan; Nie, Hua; Zeng, Huang; He, Junwei
one_liner_zh: 该研究探讨植物根提取物通过抑制TLR4等信号通路缓解类风湿关节炎，虽含分子对接和MD模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Dendropanax proteus (Champ.) Benth. root (DPR) is a traditional anti-rheumatoid arthritis (RA) plant in China. However, its bio-phytochemicals, effect, and mechanism against RA remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To explore the major bio-phytochemicals, therapeutical effect, and underlying mechanism of DPR against RA. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The therapeutical effect of DPR was measured in both collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rats and TNF-alpha-induced MH7A cells. Proteomics, metabolomics, and cell model were carried out to uncover the underlying mechanism of DPR. The major bio-phytochemicals in DPR were identified and isolated, and their anti-RA effects and mechanisms were evaluated using MH7A cells, molecular docking, and molecular dynamic simulation. RESULTS: DPR significantly alleviated paw swelling, reduced arthritis scores, and decreased serum levels of TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-17, IFN-gamma, CRP, and RF in CIA rats. DPR also inhibited inflammation and repaired cartilage damage in the ankle joint, as evidenced by hematoxylin and eosin staining, safranin O-fast green staining, Alcian blue staining, and tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase staining. Proteomic and metabolomic analyses indicated that DPR's anti-RA mechanism is associated with the inhibition of TLR4/CLEC1B/PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB pathways, as validated by Western blotting experiments. Syringin and chlorogenic acid, identified as two major phytochemicals in DPR, possess strong anti-RA effects in TNF-alpha-induced MH7A cells and good binding abilities with TLR4, Rap1, CLEC1B, PI3K, Akt, and p65 proteins. CONCLUSIONS: DPR alleviates RA by inhibiting TLR4/CLEC1B/PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB pathways, with syringin and chlorogenic acid as its major bio-phytochemicals. This study provides scientific evidence supporting the clinical use of DPR and offers potential lead compounds for the development of anti-RA agents.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性： Dendropanax proteus (Champ.) Benth. 的根（DPR）是中国传统的抗类风湿关节炎（RA）植物。然而，其生物植物化学成分、抗RA效果及机制尚不清楚。研究目的： 探讨DPR抗RA的主要生物植物化学成分、治疗效果及潜在机制。材料与方法： 在胶原诱导性关节炎（CIA）大鼠和TNF-α诱导的MH7A细胞中评估DPR的治疗效果。采用蛋白质组学、代谢组学和细胞模型揭示DPR的潜在机制。鉴定并分离DPR中的主要生物植物化学成分，并通过MH7A细胞、分子对接和分子动力学模拟评估其抗RA效果和机制。结果： DPR显著减轻CIA大鼠的足爪肿胀，降低关节炎评分，并降低血清中TNF-α、IL-1β、IL-17、IFN-γ、CRP和RF水平。苏木精-伊红染色、番红O-固绿染色、阿尔辛蓝染色和抗酒石酸酸性磷酸酶染色显示，DPR还抑制踝关节炎症并修复软骨损伤。蛋白质组学和代谢组学分析表明，DPR的抗RA机制与抑制TLR4/CLEC1B/PI3K/Akt/NF-κB通路相关，并通过Western blotting实验验证。丁香苷和绿原酸被鉴定为DPR中的两种主要植物化学成分，在TNF-α诱导的MH7A细胞中具有强抗RA效果，并与TLR4、Rap1、CLEC1B、PI3K、Akt和p65蛋白具有良好的结合能力。结论： DPR通过抑制TLR4/CLEC1B/PI3K/Akt/NF-κB通路缓解RA，其中丁香苷和绿原酸为其主要生物植物化学成分。本研究为DPR的临床应用提供了科学依据，并为开发抗RA药物提供了潜在的先导化合物。
